title: Philippine Revolution
summary: In August 1896, after a Spanish friar was tipped off about the Katipunan, a secret society of about 30,000 members, Andres Bonifacio proclaimed revolution against Spain. Sources disagree on the date and place of the first cry, 23 or 26 August at Pugad Lawin or Balintawak. Fighting was strongest in Cavite under Emilio Aguinaldo, and the revolution is dated 1896-1898.

uncertainty.note: The first cry is dated 23 August (NHCP marker) or 26 August (Library of Congress guide); the Library of Congress country study has Bonifacio attacking Spanish installations on 29 August 1896. The end year follows the Library of Congress guide span 1896-1898.

where.modern_name: Balintawak / Bahay Toro area, Quezon City, Metro Manila (disputed site of the first cry); fighting also in Cavite Province

importance.justification: The revolt against Spanish rule in the Philippines, tied in the sources to the Biak-na-Bato pact and later events.

beats.caption: After a friar was tipped off about the Katipunan, Bonifacio proclaimed revolution and attacked Spanish military installations on 29 August 1896.
Between August and November 1896 rebels commanded by Aguinaldo defeated colonial troops in Cavite, which became the centre of the revolution.
Rizal was executed on 30 December 1896; the Library of Congress study says his death filled the rebels with new determination.

reviewer_note: Date and place of the first cry are disputed in the sources (23 vs 26 August; Pugad Lawin vs Balintawak); the pin uses the Balintawak barangay as a central point. Least sure: end of revolution (1898 from LoC guide span only).
